why: All three checks pass, so the core divergence stands; only the claim's field enumeration is overstated. (1) QUOTE VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless.md, line 214, the `mcp_server_errors` row of the table under the heading 'Fail CI when a plugin or MCP server doesn't load': '...Affected servers are absent from `mcp_servers`. The key is omitted when there are no errors, so a CI gate can fail on a non-empty array. Requires Claude Code v2.1.219 or later'. Reading the whole line does not reverse the conclusion — it strengthens it (the neighbouring `plugin_errors` row at :207 carries the same 'key is omitted' rule, and the paragraph at :216 says that when stderr is captured by a CI runner Claude Code 'reports the skipped entries only in the `mcp_server_errors` field'). (2) CITED LINES: apps/cli/src/index.ts:457 `const streamJson = args.outputFormat === 'stream-json'`; :468-470 `if (streamJson) { process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(ev) + '\n') }` inside the `client.on('session:event', ...)` subscription — raw passthrough of our own wire event, confirmed; :516-535 is the `case 'complete'` arm, confirmed. `--output-format text, json, or stream-json` is advertised in the help text at :2048. (3) LAYER UP / LAYER DOWN. Absence confirmed with grep -a (NUL-byte safe) across packages, apps, docs-site and scripts: zero hits for `mcp_server_errors`, `plugin_errors`, `api_retry`; zero hits for `'init'`/`"init"`/`system/init` in apps/cli/src/index.ts. The event union itself is the proof rather than a grep: packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966-1016 (`AgentEvent`) and packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:340-375 (the wire DTO) contain no `system`/`init` member and no plugin- or MCP-load-error member of any name. Consequence verified separately from the identifiers: nothing else on the stream carries a plugin or MCP load failure either. The `info`/`status` events that do exist cover mirror errors, hook errors, compaction, fallback-model retry and agent eviction (SessionManager.ts:3693, :5442, :6601, :11307, :18011; pi-agent.ts:6337, :6384) — none names MCP or plugin loading. The one place MCP load state IS modelled, `mcpHealth {status, connected, failed}` (SessionManager.ts:3178, packages/core/src/types/pi-harness-runtime.ts:315), rides the Pi harness runtime SNAPSHOT consumed by the desktop control center, not `session:event`, and apps/cli never invokes it (the CLI's only RPCs are sessions:* / workspaces / connections / sources / plugin / doctor). Not an owner decision: none of the nine dated decisions in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md section 3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/isManagedModelAllowed, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries/foldSessionSummary) touches the headless stream shape. Not a de-brand rename either: the missing frames are capabilities, not renamed symbols. WHAT THE CLAIM GETS WRONG, and why it is a correction rather than a refutation: two of the six identifiers it lists are renames of things the stream DOES emit. The stream terminates — `complete` (dto.ts:351, handled at index.ts:516-535 where it sets `finished = true`) is our `result` — and it carries cost: `tokenUsage: Session['tokenUsage']` resolves to `TokenUsage` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:500-505) whose `costUsd: number` is required, and the agent-side `AgentEventUsage.costUsd` sits at :889. So 'no total_cost_usd or terminating result message' is true of the Claude spellings only. `capabilities`, `system/init`, `plugin_errors`, `mcp_server_errors` and `api_retry` are genuinely absent as capabilities. One more scoping fact a fixer needs: our CLI has no `--mcp-config` and no `--plugin-dir` flag (grep -a over apps/cli/src/index.ts → 0 hits), so the exact mechanism the doc's two error arrays describe has no per-run analogue here; the gap is about installed plugins and configured MCP servers, not about per-invocation config entries. Partial mitigation exists but does not close it: `nessy-general-agent doctor --json` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:180-232) exits 1 on findings and emits `unfulfilledPluginMandates`, `invalidManagedEntries`, `rejectedSettingsLayers` and `invalidAgentDefinitions`, and `plugin validate <path> --strict` exits 1 on a bad bundle — so a MANDATED-BUT-NOT-INSTALLED plugin is CI-gateable out of band. Neither covers an installed plugin that fails to load, and neither covers MCP servers at all.
correctedState: `--output-format stream-json` (apps/cli/src/index.ts:457, :468-470) writes each `session:event` verbatim, so the stream is our own protocol rather than Claude's. Genuinely missing, with no equivalent anywhere on the stream: the `system/init` frame and its `plugins`, `plugin_errors`, `mcp_servers`, `mcp_server_errors` and `capabilities` fields, and `system/api_retry` — grep -a finds none of the three error/retry identifiers in packages, apps, docs-site or scripts, and neither `AgentEvent` (packages/core/src/types/message.ts:966) nor the wire DTO (packages/shared/src/protocol/dto.ts:340-375) has a member of any name carrying a plugin or MCP load failure. The consequence holds as scoped: a CI job consuming the stream cannot see that a plugin or an MCP server failed to load. Two items in the original enumeration are renames, not absences, and should be dropped from it: the stream DOES terminate, with `complete` (dto.ts:351, handled at index.ts:516-535), and that frame DOES carry cost as `tokenUsage.costUsd` (`TokenUsage.costUsd`, packages/core/src/types/message.ts:505; `AgentEventUsage.costUsd`, :889) — only the spelling `total_cost_usd` is absent. Two scoping facts for any fix: our CLI has no `--mcp-config` or `--plugin-dir` flag, so the doc's per-invocation error classes have no direct analogue; and `nessy-general-agent doctor --json` already exits 1 with `unfulfilledPluginMandates` (apps/cli/src/doctor.ts:219-222), giving an out-of-band CI gate for mandated-but-not-installed plugins — but not for an installed plugin that fails to load, and not for MCP servers, whose only load state (`mcpHealth {status, connected, failed}`, SessionManager.ts:3178) lives in the Pi harness snapshot the CLI never queries.
